Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widgets

Class CalendarDef

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widgets.CalendarDef
All Implemented Interfaces:
Widget
public class CalendarDef extends Object implements Widget
A reusable month-calendar definition: month/year navigation, event categories, and a display-only legend (parent concept #10).

This is the Widget marker type — the juneau-rest-server-widgets org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widgets.Widget, not org.apache.juneau.marshall.html.HtmlWidget (the unrelated $W{...} HTML header-widget SPI). It is bean-only: the emitter (CalendarTable) and the juneau-calendar.js/.css runtime live in juneau-rest-server-views, which composes this bean. Widgets keeps no dependency on views.

The server renders the initial month grid + legend and paints real seed chips into the day cells (progressive enhancement); the runtime then computes each month client-side and hydrates events from a same-origin, data-only per-month GET whose envelope is {contractVersion, year, month, events}. When endpoint is null the calendar is seed-only and month navigation is disabled.

Since:
10.0.0

  • Field Details

    • CONTRACT_VERSION

      public static final String CONTRACT_VERSION
      The frozen contract version for the per-month event GET envelope and the stamped data-juneau-calendar-contract attribute. Serialized as the JSON string "2" (a numeric 2 would fail the client's strict === handshake).

      Bumped from "1" to "2" for the end-becomes-layout-significant change even though the envelope gained no new required field (end was already carried for forward-compat). The bump is justified because this same constant is the stamped data-juneau-calendar-contract attribute: a v1 runtime paired with a v2 server would silently ignore end and paint a multi-day event as a single chip, so making the handshake fail loud is the point. Do not copy this as a general pattern — a wire contract that is not also a runtime-handshake stamp should not bump for a no-new-field change.

      See Also:

    • MAX_LANES_PER_WEEK

      public static final int MAX_LANES_PER_WEEK
      The hard internal ceiling on spanning-bar lanes in one week row.

      The lane budget is derived from effectiveMaxPerDay() and clamped here; it is deliberately not author-controllable (there is no maxLanesPerWeek bean field). Bars that would need a lane beyond the budget are collapsed into the day cells' "+N more" affordance instead of stacking a week row arbitrarily tall.

    • effectiveLaneBudget

      public int effectiveLaneBudget()
      The per-week-row spanning-bar lane budget — effectiveMaxPerDay() clamped to MAX_LANES_PER_WEEK.

      Spanning bars occupy lanes counted against this budget; maxPerDay itself continues to cap the non-spanning chips (single-day all-day plus timed) inside a day cell. The two caps are separate on purpose: a bar crossing a cell does not consume that cell's chip budget, and a hidden chip does not consume a lane.

      Returns:
      The derived lane budget, at least 1 and at most MAX_LANES_PER_WEEK.

    • validate

      Description copied from interface: Widget
      Fail-closed bean validation.
      Specified by:

    • validate

      public void validate(Integer effectiveYear, Integer effectiveMonth)
      Fail-closed bean validation against a resolved (year, month) window.

      When initialYear/initialMonth are unset, the emitter resolves the effective window from the injected clock and passes it here so seed events are still checked against the month actually rendered.

      Parameters:
      effectiveYear - The year the initial month is rendered for, or null to skip the off-month check.
      effectiveMonth - The 1-based month rendered, or null to skip the off-month check.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If this definition is not well-formed.
